evidence: books/peer-pull.lisp:503-509: `((fn-pull-msgidp line) (let ((listed (fn-pull-list (fn-pull-r-listed r)))) (mv (fn-pull-with r :listed (if (member-equal line listed) listed (append listed (list line)))) nil t)))`; close at :700-707 `fn-pull-all-answered-or-unavailablep` calls `(fn-pull-answer-of (car listed) answers)` = `assoc-equal` over all answers for each listed id, and fn-pull-completep/fn-pull-close/fn-pull-close-effects/fn-pull-dropped each re-evaluate it.
fix: Keep listed ids in a hashed or trie set (or reuse the Message-ID trie machinery) with an append-at-tail accumulator. Keep answers in a map keyed by id. Process the listing in bounded batches (offer and fetch as ids stream in, with the cursor still ack-bounded), so the per-step work is bounded and the round state does not grow with the peer's list.
reviewer: books/peer-pull.lisp:503-509: in the :list phase, every msgid line does member-equal over listed and then append to its end, which is O(n) per line and O(n^2) for the listing. Nothing caps the listing length. The only bounds are the per-line :long check (fn-pull-split-aux :178) and the per-chunk read limit (peer-pull-session.lisp:811-813), and neither limits the number of lines. At close, fn-pull-all-answered-or-unavailablep (:700-707) does an assoc-equal over answers plus a member-equal over unavailable for each listed id, which is O(n*m). The first round asks for a 24h window (*fn-pull-first-window-ms* :71). Medium rather than high because pull peers are operator-configured, but a large honest listing still stalls the single pull worker.
scenario: A peer answers NEWNEWS with 200,000 ids. This is a normal day for a busy upstream, and the first round asks a 24-hour window (*fn-pull-first-window-ms*); a hostile peer can list millions. Each line costs O(listed) for member-equal plus an O(listed) append, so about 2e10 list comparisons and conses happen inside the pull worker before a single IHAVE. The whole list is then held in the round state, and the close does a further O(listed x answers) at least three times. D27's 'bound work per scheduling step' is violated, and the single pull worker (and the catch-up rounds that share it) stalls for hours.
title: NEWNEWS listing is unbounded and quadratic: member-equal plus append per listed id, then an assoc per id at close
